profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] DartPoints own company site describes a strategy of delivering enterprise grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure services to communities outside the largest United States metros, operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets. The company began operations in the early 2000s and received a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025. DartPoints is headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas. The company own site lists 11 facilities including Baton Rouge, Louisiana (2 facilities) and Shreveport, Louisiana; Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio; Columbus, Indiana; Asheville, North Carolina; and Columbia, Greenville, Charleston, and Spartanburg, South Carolina, matching every state where this registry lists a DartPoints facility. The South Carolina registry row listed as Ladson likely corresponds to the Charleston area market named on the company site, since Ladson is a suburb of Charleston, though this specific building was not individually confirmed. The company emphasizes AI ready, high density infrastructure, 99.999 percent uptime, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. No building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
The published IT capacity for DartPoints Dublin is 3 MW. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 3 MW of IT load is roughly 75 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a colocation baseline, the same load supports roughly 300 racks. The operator has not published power-usage effectiveness, cooling architecture, or fiber connectivity details on the spec page this site read, so no further inference about AI suitability can be drawn from the numbers alone.

The spec page lists a Dublin, Ohio address in its URL, but the structured address field records 601 Milam St., Shreveport, LA 71101, and the postal code confirms Louisiana. The data contains a direct conflict between the city, state, and URL on one hand and the street address on the other. This site cannot resolve that conflict from published facts, and the reading below treats the state context as given for Ohio while noting the discrepancy.

Among the 76 Ohio facilities this site has mapped, only 3 have published a megawatt figure, and their combined published capacity is 26 MW. At 3 MW, this campus ranks third among those three, contributing roughly 12 percent of the published Ohio total. That share reflects the sparsity of published data, not a complete picture of Ohio capacity, since most mapped facilities publish no figure. At 3 MW, the campus is small relative to hyperscale AI training deployments, which commonly require tens to hundreds of megawatts, but it sits within a range that can support inference workloads or smaller training clusters if the power and cooling infrastructure qualify.
